messages:
priya: Heads-up: PR #447 (migration guide + SDK snippets) is blocked by a runtime clarification and a linkcheck failure. Runtime: need the canonical default for `compat_mode` so we can decide whether snippets should set it explicitly.

alex: short summary from runtime: hosted API default = true (backcompat). We plan to make it opt-in-deprecate in a future release. Dedicated/private may be operator-configured and could differ.

maria: thanks. If hosted default is going away, we should show explicit setting in the migration example rather than depending on the default. That avoids surprising customers.

sam-runtime: agree. Also call out the subtle behavior change: with compat_mode=true we use legacy context trimming which can keep older prefixes and increases token accounting; compat_mode=false uses a sliding token window optimized for throughput.

priya: can you give me a one-line sentence I can paste under the migration note that captures that? Need something concise and non-technical for the doc.

aslex: oops typo, meant alex.

alex: pasteable line: "Hosted customers: compat_mode defaults to true to preserve legacy request semantics; we recommend passing compat_mode explicitly during migration because this default is scheduled for deprecation. Dedicated/private defaults can vary by operator."

maria: good. For the migration section I want a 1-line user-facing note about the trimming behavior. Sam, can you write that in plain English?

sam-runtime: sure: "When compat_mode is true, the service preserves legacy context-trimming behavior (which may keep older parts of the conversation and increase token usage); when false, a newer token-window trimming is used to reduce tokens and improve throughput."

priya: ok i'll add both lines and switch the Python and JS snippets to include the explicit flag. Example Python will show compat_mode=True for the legacy migration path.

maria: quick CI note: doc-bot linkcheck flagged two broken anchors in /migration/compatibility.md (#sdk-examples, #old-examples). Those need to be fixed before preview will be green.

doc-bot: linkcheck: 2 broken anchors found in /migration/compatibility.md -> #sdk-examples, #old-examples. Full: "ERROR linkcheck: broken anchors"

priya: i'll patch the anchors and push. Hold merge until linkcheck passes and alex gives runtime +1.

alex: ping me once preview shows new wording and I'll review.

maria: also confirm whether we should call out Dedicated override precedence in the migration note. I'd rather be explicit: operator settings beat hosted defaults.

sam-runtime: confirmed: operator-configured defaults (Dedicated/private) take precedence over hosted default. Add that sentence.

priya: perfect. I'll update PR, fix anchors, rerun preview. Will report back here with preview link.

doc-bot: preview updated: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-447 (linkcheck queued)

alex: thanks all.
